title: Larger-Register Complexity of Carlet et al. S-Box Masking
summary: The countermeasure appears to retain exponential-in-k, quadratic-in-n time even with large registers; whether larger registers can improve it remains open.

formal_statement.body: The Carlet et al. higher-order S-box masking countermeasure performs its computations in the field $\mathbb{F}_{2^k}$ and is described as having complexity $O(2^{k/2} \cdot n^2)$, with no established benefit from using larger registers. Determine whether this countermeasure can exploit larger register sizes and, if so, characterize the resulting time complexity as a function of the relevant parameters $k$, $n$, and register size.

scope.domain: Time complexity of the Carlet et al. higher-order S-box masking countermeasure over a binary extension field.
parameters: k: extension degree and exponent-driving complexity parameter
n: parameter contributing the quadratic complexity factor
register size: machine-register width whose potential complexity benefit is unresolved
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine whether larger registers can be exploited and, if so, characterize the resulting time complexity in terms of k, n, and register size.

citations.label: Higher Order Masking of Look-Up Tables

progress.summary: The paper explicitly says it is unclear how the field-based countermeasure could benefit from larger registers and suggests that its stated complexity therefore persists even for large registers.
citation_labels: Jean-Sébastien Coron et al., Higher Order Masking of Look-Up Tables
